content.value_statement: Agent frameworks often hide how context, memory, and token budgets interact. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured way to inspect memory flow and compare design choices.
actual_capabilities: Breaks down standard prompt assembly order for agent systems.
Compares template, chat message, and programmatic assembly patterns.
Evaluates FIFO, sliding window, summarization, vector, and importance-based eviction policies.
Maps working, session, and persistent memory tiers.
Reviews token counting methods and budget allocation choices.
Provides a structured report format for memory architecture analysis.
limitations: Provides analysis guidance, not runnable tooling or automatic code scanning.
Examples are illustrative and must be adapted to each framework.
Does not benchmark real retrieval quality or model performance.
Does not implement databases, vector stores, or tokenizers.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Framework Memory
use_cases.description: Trace how an agent framework builds prompts, stores history, and handles context overflow.

use_cases.title: Compare Context Strategies
use_cases.description: Compare memory tiers, eviction policies, and token allocation across multiple agent designs.

use_cases.title: Document State Continuity Risks
use_cases.description: Create a clear report on where user preferences, summaries, or retrieved memories may be lost.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Prompt Assembly
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one agent framework.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use memory-orchestration to inspect this agent framework. Identify how the system prompt, tools, history, memory, and current input are assembled.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Context Overflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of history trimming behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the context overflow strategy. Identify the eviction trigger, what content is removed, and what user experience risks it creates.

prompt_templates.title: Map Memory Tiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the working, session, and persistent memory tiers. Explain storage location, retrieval method, capacity assumptions, and failure risks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Production Strategies
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison across frameworks or implementations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the memory orchestration strategies in these agent systems. Rank prompt assembly, eviction, persistence, and token budget choices by operational risk.

output_examples.input: Review how this support agent preserves customer context during long conversations.
output_examples.output: The analysis identifies a sliding window policy with no summary fallback. It explains where older customer details may be dropped during overflow.

output_examples.input: Compare memory handling between two agent frameworks.
output_examples.output: The result compares assembly order, memory tiers, eviction triggers, and token budget allocation. It highlights which design better preserves state continuity.

output_examples.input: Document the memory architecture for a new agent platform.
output_examples.output: The report describes working memory, session history, persistent storage, retrieval flow, and overflow handling in a concise architecture format.

best_practices: Review actual prompt assembly paths before judging memory behavior.
Separate short-term conversation history from persistent user memory.
Reserve output tokens before filling the context window with history.
anti_patterns: Assuming recent messages are always the most important context.
Storing all conversation history without retention or privacy rules.
Using summaries without checking what details they remove.

faq.question: Does this skill run code?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis steps and report structure for reviewing existing agent framework code or designs.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it choose an eviction policy?
faq.answer: It can compare tradeoffs, but final policy selection depends on product needs, privacy rules, and model limits.

faq.question: Does it require a vector database?
faq.answer: No. Vector stores are only one memory tier option covered by the analysis.

faq.question: Can it analyze token budgets?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews counting methods, fixed allocations, output reserve, and overflow behavior.

faq.question: Is it useful for non-code architecture reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. The framework can document design choices even when source code is unavailable.
